existingReportSummary.executiveSummaryMd: `AllergyIntolerance` has material local breaking changes despite stable resource identity. The top migration concerns are remapping `lastOccurrence`, converting `reaction.manifestation` to `CodeableReference`, and converting primitive `type` values into `CodeableConcept`; the main uncertainty is terminology expansion confirmation for verification-status codes.
existingReportSummary.migrationThemesMd: Migration is mainly a JSON/model-shape problem plus an R6-to-R4 lossiness problem. R4-to-R6 transforms should rename `lastOccurrence`, wrap `reaction.manifestation` CodeableConcepts under `CodeableReference.concept`, and wrap `type` primitive codes as CodeableConcept codings. R6-to-R4 transforms need policies for Observation-backed manifestations, non-value-set `type` CodeableConcepts, `verificationStatus=presumed`, missing or otherwise R4-invalid `clinicalStatus` combinations, and `recorder` references to `Organization`.
existingReportSummary.confidenceSummaryMd: Confidence is high for structural changes because both StructureDefinitions are present and directly comparable. Confidence is medium for exact terminology membership of R6 terminology.hl7.org systems because expansions and R6 CodeSystem artifacts for allergyintolerance clinical/verification status were not available locally; the `presumed` finding is supported by the R6 StructureDefinition short text and ConceptMap rather than by a local expansion.

compatibilityLeverage.note: Resource-level leverage is a planning signal. It does not mark individual Revisit findings as justified or unimportant.

rationaleMd:
AllergyIntolerance keeps its resource identity. The aggregate has 3 hard R4-to-R6 instance break(s), 0 potential hard break(s), 1 non-mechanical migration finding(s), and 2 direct behavior/API finding(s).

R4 maturity context is trial-use/FMM 3, which creates meaningful stability pressure.

The computed migration-unavoidability score is 46/100, producing migration shape `moderate-targeted-remodel`, major migration `Partial`, and compatibility posture `preserve-where-low-cost-but-expect-resource-migration`.

4 finding(s) identify a yes/partial less-breaking base-design alternative, so the aggregate should not be used to dismiss local avoidability review.

11 shared Resource/DomainResource behavior finding(s) are listed as context but not scored for this resource to avoid duplicating base behavior issues across all resources.
recommendedStandardsPostureMd: Expect targeted migration work, but continue reviewing individual breaks. Use less-breaking designs where they do not preserve obsolete or conflicting models indefinitely.

topFindings.title: AllergyIntolerance.lastOccurrence was replaced by lastReactionOccurrence
topFindings.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: an R4 instance containing `lastOccurrence` uses a property R6 does not define; generated models, FHIRPath, serializers, and reverse R6-to-R4 exchange also need explicit renaming.
topFindings.whyRelevant: Owned by this resource's StructureDefinition report.

topFindings.title: AllergyIntolerance.type changed from required primitive code to preferred CodeableConcept
topFindings.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: a present R4 `type` string such as `allergy` is not the R6 `CodeableConcept` object shape; R6 preferred-bound text or non-legacy codings are also lossy or invalid when converted back to R4.
topFindings.whyRelevant: Owned by this resource's StructureDefinition report.

topFindings.title: reaction.manifestation changed from CodeableConcept to CodeableReference(Observation)
topFindings.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: a direct R4 manifestation item with `coding`/`text` is not the R6 `CodeableReference` shape unless wrapped under `concept`; additionally, R6 `Observation` references create R6-to-R4 loss.
